Background: US9769907B2 (assigned to BASF SE) describes a positive electrode active material in which a conventional arrangement is used. That approach does not resolve the low intrinsic electronic conductivity of olivine phosphates. The present application instead relies on carbon-coated LiFe(1-x)MnxPO4 particles wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.45 and the carbon coating has a thickness of 2 nm to 6 nm.

output.text: US9769907B2, assigned to BASF SE, discloses a positive electrode active material comprising a conventional arrangement, yet such configurations fail to overcome the characteristically low intrinsic electronic conductivity of olivine phosphates. To address this deficiency, materials may comprise carbon-coated LiFe(1-x)MnxPO4 particles, wherein 0.15 <= x <= 0.45, with a carbon coating having a thickness in a range of 2 nm to 6 nm.

Technical Field: The present disclosure relates to silicon-composite anodes.
Abstract: There is provided a negative electrode for a lithium secondary battery comprising a silicon-carbon composite in which silicon domains of 5 nm to 30 nm are dispersed within a porous carbon scaffold. The disclosure thereby addresses capacity fade caused by the ~300% volume expansion of silicon on lithiation.

output.text: A negative electrode for a lithium secondary battery is provided to address capacity fade associated with the ~300% volume expansion of silicon on lithiation. The electrode comprises a silicon-carbon composite wherein silicon domains having a size of 5 nm to 30 nm are dispersed within a porous carbon scaffold, thereby accommodating said volume expansion.

Abstract: A method of beam management in a wireless network is disclosed. The method of beam management in a wireless network comprises selecting an analog beam from a hierarchical codebook based on a reported layer-1 reference signal received power for each of at least four candidate beams. The disclosed arrangement addresses the pilot overhead and latency of exhaustive beam sweeping in large antenna arrays.

Technical Field: The present disclosure relates to proton-exchange-membrane water electrolysis.
Abstract: There is provided a membrane electrode assembly for water electrolysis comprising an anode catalyst layer having an iridium loading of 0.15 mg/cm2 to 0.35 mg/cm2 supported on antimony-doped tin oxide. The disclosure thereby addresses the scarcity of iridium at the anode limiting terawatt-scale electrolyser deployment.

output.text: A membrane electrode assembly for proton-exchange-membrane water electrolysis is provided, comprising an anode catalyst layer wherein an iridium loading of 0.15 mg/cm2 to 0.35 mg/cm2 is supported on antimony-doped tin oxide. Such a configuration addresses the scarcity of iridium at the anode, a factor that limits terawatt-scale electrolyser deployment.
